**Unitary authority with the greatest drop in domestic gas consumption (2012 → 2023)**  

| Authority | 2012 consumption (GWh) | 2023 consumption (GWh) | Drop (kWh) |
|-----------|-----------------------|------------------------|------------|
| Bedford | 979.916949 GWh | 657.806202 GWh | 322,110,747 kWh |
| County Durham | 883.754565 GWh | 775.471657 GWh | 108,282,908 kWh |
| Flintshire | 978.7055 GWh | 928.943159 GWh | 49,762,341 kWh |
| North Lincolnshire | 828.9919 GWh | 774.823850 GWh | 54,168,050 kWh |
| Telford & Wrekin | 198.363245 GWh | 339.590080 GWh | –141,226,835 kWh (increase) |

**Result**

Bedford experienced the largest decline in domestic gas consumption, falling by **approximately 322 million kWh** between 2012 and 2023.

*Evidence* – These figures come from the Office of National Statistics (ONS) dataset *gas_LA_stacked_2005‑2024.csv*, which records domestic gas consumption (in GWh) for each lower-tier/local authority for each year. The 2012 and 2023 rows for Bedford show 979.916949 GWh and 657.806202 GWh respectively, giving a drop of 322.110747 GWh = 322,110,747 kWh. The other authorities display smaller drops; Telford & Wrekin actually increased consumption.
